newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks slide sharply on selling.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks slide sharply on selling.

text.p: Cyprus stocks slid sharply in the first two trading days of the week, losing 1.6 percent of their value on investor selling, traders said.
The Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) 41-share general index retreated on Wednesday to close at 80.83 points from its closing level of 82.15 on Friday.
On Tuesday alone the market fell by 1.31 percent. The market was closed on Monday for the Epiphany holiday.
"A small number of investors realised their profits while there was no interest on the part of buyers," explained Christodoulos Ellinas of Share Link.

He said trading on the market was still muted after the Christmas and New Year holiday lull, and dismissed suggestions the decline could have been sparked by new tension in the region between Cyprus and Turkey after the Cypriot government's decision to buy anti-aircraft missiles from Russia.
Banking shares slid to 89.88 on Wednesday from 91.68 on Friday. Fully paid shares in the Bank of Cyprus closed at 336.5, slipping 7.5 cents from Friday.
Fully paid shares of the Cyprus Popular Bank closed at 324.5, going down six cents from Fridays closing price. The Hellenic Bank dropped four cents, closing at 260.5.
Universal Savings Bank shares remained steady at 138.5.

Approved investment stocks went down 2.09 percent and its sub-index closed at 72.96 on Wednesday. Shares in Era Portfolio Investments slid three cents, closing at 127.5. Cytrustees shares slipped three cents to close at 149.
Insurance stocks also declined, closing at 56.96 points from 57.79 on Friday.
Universal Life shares dropped one cent, closing at 368. Paneuropean Insurance fully paid lost two cents, closing at 121.5.
Cement producer Vassiliko closed at 159.5, dropping half a cent. Beer and wine producers Keo retreated 1.5 cents to close at 114.
